cards.heading: Definition
cards.question: What is per-product agent runtime isolation?
cards.answer: Running each AI product on its own dedicated agent-runtime stack (own server process, database, cache) instead of one centralized runtime shared across the organization, so each squad owns the latency, cost, and incident response for its own agents.

cards.heading: Organisational rationale
cards.question: What is the organisational rationale for giving each squad its own agent runtime?
cards.answer: You-build-it-you-run-it: a squad's accountability for the latency, cost, and pager duty of its agents is only credible if the squad actually controls the runtime it built on.

cards.heading: Blast-radius rationale
cards.question: What is the blast-radius rationale for per-product runtime isolation?
cards.answer: A shared central agent runtime is a systemic single point of failure — one bad deploy or one resource-hungry agent degrades every agent in the company at once. Per-product stacks confine an incident to a single use case.

cards.heading: What prevents N snowflakes
cards.question: What stops per-product runtime isolation from turning into N different snowflake configurations?
cards.answer: Every product starts from the same templated runtime configuration — allow-listed base image, corporate certificate bundle, standard routes. Isolation without that shared template just multiplies drift.

cards.heading: The admitted cost
cards.question: What cost does the team openly admit comes with running per-product agent runtimes?
cards.answer: More infrastructure to operate and more upgrades to coordinate (more charts to upgrade, more versions to pin) — named as their next, still-unsolved investment area.
